readings.text: Let the wise hear and increase in learning, and the one who understands obtain guidance.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.

devotionals.word:
Zoom is the move that steps back. All week you've been close to the words, nose to the page. Zoom says push the chair back and look at the whole table.

Perspective is the virtue, and it's what you get when you see a thing from far enough away. One verse looks like a loose thread. Pull back to the whole book, the whole story, and that thread is holding something together.

The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. That one word, beginning, only makes sense from the height. Knowledge doesn't start with what you already know. It starts with admitting you don't, and looking up.

Paul says the same thing wide. Rightly handling the word of truth. Not your word. Not the one verse you like. The truth, the whole long story, from the garden to the city at the end.

Tomorrow the year begins, one day at a time. But today, see the whole of it first. Seven moves, one habit. Zoom is the move that remembers where the road is going.
devotionals.apply: Before the year starts, picture the whole of it. Seven moves, repeated every week for a year. You won't do it all at once and you won't do it alone. Zoom out, then step back in.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, lift my eyes to the whole story. Give me the perspective to see this year as one long walk with you, not a sprint. Amen.

devotionals.word:
Flow is the move that listens for rhythm. Not music, exactly. The way things move and repeat and turn. A river doesn't push. It keeps going, patient, and it wears down whatever won't move.

Proverbs has a current you can feel once you stop trying to master it in one sitting. The words step one after another, and if you rush you miss the movement under them.

Patience is the virtue because flow can't be hurried. You learn a language by hearing it long before you speak it. You learn a river by walking beside it, not by jumping in and demanding it go faster.

Paul's word for Timothy is rightly, and rightly is a slow word. A worker in a hurry cuts corners. A patient worker measures twice and cuts once, and the work holds.

So today don't try to finish anything. Sit with the rhythm and let it move past you. That isn't wasted time. It's how you learn to read anything that matters.
devotionals.apply: Read the passage out loud, slowly, twice. Listen for a word or phrase that comes back. That repetition is the current. Sit with it for a minute before you go.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, slow me down. Teach me the patience to let your word move at its own pace, and to move with it. Amen.

devotionals.word:
Shape is the move that asks how the pieces fit. A verse on its own is a loose board. It only starts to mean something when you see where it sits in the whole house.

Clarity is the virtue, because a shape that fits is a thing you can finally see. Proverbs doesn't drop one verse and walk away. It builds. Wisdom leads to instruction, instruction to understanding, understanding to the fear of the LORD. There's an order to it, a frame holding it together.

Most of us read the Bible like a box of puzzle pieces with no picture on the lid. We pull out a verse, spin it, set it down, pull out another. Shape says stop and find the picture first. What is this piece attached to, and where does it go?

Paul hands Timothy a shape too. Handle the word of truth rightly. A worker who handles something rightly knows what it's for, because he's seen the whole thing, not just the part in his hand.

You won't see all of it today. The move is just the question. Where does this fit, and what's it connected to?
devotionals.apply: Take today's verse and read the sentence right before it and the sentence right after it. Notice how the middle one sits between them. That's the shape starting to show.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, give me eyes for how the pieces fit. Show me the whole shape of your word, not just the fragments. Amen.

readings.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.

devotionals.word:
Counting gets a bad name. People hear it and think of math tests and ledger books. But counting is simpler than that, and harder. It's how you tell what's actually big and what's actually small, and most of the time you can't do it by feel. You have to put a number on it and look.

Proverbs opens with a list, and a list is made to be counted. Wisdom, instruction, understanding, righteousness, justice, equity, prudence, knowledge, discretion. Nine different things, and none of them stands in for the others. Counting slows you down enough to see each one.

The virtue behind Count is honesty. When you count, you agree to see what's there, not what you wish was there. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. Beginning, not the whole thing. Counting keeps you honest about where you actually are, and that's the only place learning can start.

Paul gives it to Timothy in one word. Rightly. Rightly handling the word of truth. Rightly means measured and accurate, not sloppy. You can't handle something rightly if you refuse to look at how big it is.
devotionals.apply: Open Proverbs 1 and count the different things the first seven verses promise. Write them down. Notice which one you've never stopped to think about. That one is where you start.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, make me honest about where I actually am. Teach me to count what's real and not what I wish were real. Amen.
